hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? is there a song or a poem you’ve loved so long you could say it in your sleep?
options: keep it humming. today is about a love like that.
that’s okay. today, one you might keep.

steps.line: The Prophet ﷺ once sent a man to lead a small expedition. Each time he led their prayer, he ended his recitation the same way.
With one short surah, four lines long: “Say: He is God, the One.” Every single time.

steps.q: When they got home, his companions mentioned it. What do you think the Prophet ﷺ said?
steps.why: He asked why, first. Before praising or correcting, he wanted the man’s own reason.

steps.line: “Ask him why he does it,” the Prophet ﷺ said. The man answered: “Because it describes the Most Merciful, and I love to recite it.”
“Tell him,” the Prophet ﷺ said, “that God loves him.”

steps.q: This surah is called al-Ikhlas. What does ikhlas mean?
steps.why: Ikhlas means sincerity, a heart kept pure for God. The man’s plain love for it was exactly that.

steps.q: Why might the Prophet ﷺ have said “ask him why” before anything else?
o: He wanted to correct him gently
To make him explain himself to all
The reason in his heart mattered most
steps.why: The same habit can come from hurry or from love. Asking why found the love.

steps.line: It sits near the very end of the Qur’an, in its last thirtieth, juz’ ‘amma, where the short surahs are. That’s where almost everyone starts.
Today, a five-year-old and her grandmother know the same few surahs by heart. Al-Fatiha first, then the short ones, starting from the back.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Besides “He is God, the One,” what else do the surah’s four short lines say?
o: He neither has a child nor was born
He made the heavens in six days
He forgives all who turn back to Him
steps.why: “He begets not, nor was He begotten, and there is none like Him.” Four lines, the whole idea of oneness.

say: here’s what i love. the man didn’t defend himself with an argument. he just said, i love it. and that was enough.
in islam, the qur’an runs roughly longest to shortest. children learn from the back, where the short surahs are, and many pray with them for a lifetime.

steps.line: And three weeks in, you know the words a Muslim day is built from: bismillah, salaam, alhamdulillah, ahad. The foothills, done.
steps.label: today

steps.q: The surah is tiny, yet a saying says it equals a third of the Qur’an. From this lesson, what makes it so weighty?
o: How slowly it’s meant to be recited
It was the first surah revealed
steps.why: Tawhid, God’s oneness, is what the rest of the Qur’an rests on. The first revealed was actually Iqra, “Read!”

today.say: today, listen to surah al-ikhlas once. it takes about fifteen seconds. it’s your choice: just listen, learn its first line, “qul huwa allahu ahad,” say: He is God, the One, or recite it if you already know it.
options: lovely. fifteen seconds, and bilal’s word inside.
beautiful. it’s where so many start.

sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 7375; Sahih Muslim 813 (‘A’isha: the Prophet sent a man in command of a party; he led them in prayer and ended with “Qul huwa Allahu ahad”; “Ask him why he does that”; “because it is the description of the Most Merciful and I love to recite it”; “Tell him that Allah loves him”)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5013 (al-Ikhlas equals a third of the Qur’an)
Qur’an 112:1-4 (“Say: He is Allah, the One!”)
Qur’an 78:1 (‘amma yatasa’alun, which names juz’ ‘amma, surahs 78-114)
